tools.name: crypto_quant_guide

tools.name: market_derivatives

tools.name: hyperliquid_whale_read

tools.name: formula_evaluate
tools.description: Evaluate a Basis formula expression over a loaded window. Functions are listed by catalog_search kind=formula; series named open, high, low, close, volume, returns and more. Multi-line with `let` bindings is supported; the last expression is the result.

tools.name: backtest_run
tools.description: Backtest one built-in strategy with one set of parameters. Fills happen at the next bar's open and costs are charged per side. Returns risk-adjusted metrics alongside the raw return — judge on those, not on total return.

tools.name: strategy_research
tools.description: Run one chronological research experiment across many built-in strategies, instruments and timeframes. tools.name: position_calculate
tools.description: Risk-first position sizing with quantity, notional, margin, effective leverage, fees, funding, breakeven, liquidation estimate, target R multiples and warnings. Use position_plan_on_chart instead when the user should see the plan on the chart.

tools.name: trade_experience_retrieve
tools.description: Retrieve compact historical trade analogues for the current market state. Plans are deterministic synthetic templates, while fills, stop/target ordering, MAE/MFE and outcomes are settled on later historical candles with costs. Use it to compare similar wins and failures, never as proof of an edge.

tools.name: news_recent
tools.description: Recent crypto headlines with an impact score and the assets each one touches. Impact is a keyword heuristic, not a judgement about the market.

tools.name: news_detect_assets
tools.description: Which crypto assets a piece of text refers to. Word-bounded, so "button" does not match TON and "operation" does not match OP.

tools.name: chart_state
tools.description: The chart you are building for this person: venue, symbol, timeframe, chart type, every indicator with its instance id and parameters, and every drawing. tools.name: chart_set_instrument
tools.description: Point the chart at a market. Venue and symbol as the exchange writes them, e.g. BTCUSDT on binance. This changes the chart you are building, which the person opens through chart_link.

tools.name: chart_set_timeframe
tools.description: Change the chart timeframe, e.g. 15m, 1h, 4h, 1d. Changes the chart you are building; call chart_link when you are done so the person can open it.

tools.name: chart_set_type
tools.description: Change how price is drawn — candles, heikin ashi, line, renko, footprint and others. A wrong id is refused, and the refusal lists every one that works. Changes the chart you are building; call chart_link when you are done so the person can open it.

tools.name: chart_add_indicator
tools.description: Put an indicator on the chart. studyId is an id or a common name ("ema20", "bollinger"); catalog_describe lists parameters. Omitted ones use the default. Changes the chart you are building; call chart_link when you are done so the person can open it.

tools.name: chart_update_indicator
tools.description: Edit the parameters of an existing indicator instance. First call chart_state to get its instance id; use catalog_describe for supported parameters. tools.name: chart_remove_indicator

tools.name: chart_toggle_indicator
tools.description: Hide or show an indicator without removing it — useful for comparing a chart with and without something. Changes the chart you are building; call chart_link when you are done so the person can open it.

tools.name: drawing_add

Use it to keep several drawings apart — a measured level and a projected one should not be the same colour, and a reader has only the picture to tell them by. tools.name: drawing_delete
tools.description: Delete a drawing. This cannot be undone — the shape is not recoverable — so the user is asked first. Changes the chart you are building; call chart_link when you are done so the person can open it.

tools.name: screener_run
tools.description: Scan the venue's listed instruments for ones matching conditions, instead of looking at the open chart. Every row states where its date came from — live, a published rule, an estimate, or the user

tools.description: Aggressor-side order flow: buy and sell volume separated by who crossed the spread, delta, the footprint by price level, the point of control, and absorption or stacked imbalance. Measured from the venue aggressor tag, not inferred from bar direction — use it when the question is who is being aggres

tools.name: news_history
tools.description: Read archived crypto headlines, newest first, with source links. Use news_recent for live headlines. Paginate with nextBefore (ISO timestamp). Archive coverage starts when Basis began collecting; an empty page does not prove no news occurred. No full article text.

tools.description: Reconstruct historical calendar conventions (options expiry, CME settlement, payroll schedule). NOT an archive of confirmed releases or actual economic values. Holiday exceptions may differ. No historical funding, halving, FOMC or CPI feed. Use calendar_upcoming for future events.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: chart_link, alert_link · Private data: hyperliquid_whale_read · Public sink: market_dominance, market_derivatives, calendar_upcoming, chart_link · Destructive: indicator_compute, backtest_run, strategy_research, chart_update_indicator, chart_remove_indicator, drawing_delete, screener_run, daytrade_opportunity_scan, alert_link.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: chart_link, alert_link · Private data: hyperliquid_whale_read · Public sink: market_dominance, market_derivatives, calendar_upcoming, chart_link · Destructive: indicator_compute, backtest_run, strategy_research, chart_update_indicator, chart_remove_indicator, drawing_delete, screener_run, daytrade_opportunity_scan, alert_link

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
